root_cause.text: In `block/bio-integrity-auto.c:bio_integrity_prep()`, the auto integrity buffer allocation only zero-initialized metadata when `csum_type == BLK_INTEGRITY_CSUM_NONE`, so write requests with generated PI and `metadata_size > pi_tuple_size` left the non-PI tail of each metadata tuple uninitialized.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `else if (bi->csum_type == BLK_INTEGRITY_CSUM_NONE)` to `else if (bi->metadata_size > bi->pi_tuple_size) gfp |= __GFP_ZERO;`, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that when PI is generated and the metadata size exceeds the PI tuple size, the remaining “opaque” metadata was left uninitialized and could be read back.

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero integrity metadata allocations whenever metadata extends beyond the PI tuple size, fixing incorrect dependence on checksum type.
intent_record.what: In bio_integrity_prep(), the condition for adding __GFP_ZERO to gfp in the non-IP checksum path was changed from checking bi->csum_type == BLK_INTEGRITY_CSUM_NONE to checking whether bi->metadata_size is greater than bi->pi_tuple_size.
intent_record.how: At runtime, zero-initialization of the allocated integrity metadata buffer now occurs when the metadata contains bytes beyond the protection information tuple size, rather than only when no checksum type is configured. This ensures any extra metadata area is cleared before use, preventing uninitialized trailing metadata from being exposed or consumed incorrectly.

grouping_result.intent: Zero integrity metadata allocations whenever metadata extends beyond the PI tuple size, fixing incorrect dependence on checksum type.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by zero-initializing integrity metadata based on whether metadata_size exceeds the PI tuple size, instead of incorrectly keying that behavior on csum_type.

candidates.rationale: This conditional wrongly tied zero-initialization of the integrity metadata buffer to checksum type alone. As a result, when metadata_size exceeded pi_tuple_size for write requests with generated PI and a checksum type other than NONE, the allocation was not zeroed and the non-PI tail remained uninitialized.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition made zero-initialization of the integrity metadata buffer depend only on csum_type being BLK_INTEGRITY_CSUM_NONE. When metadata_size exceeded the PI tuple size for write requests with generated PI and a different checksum type, the buffer was not zeroed, leaving the non-PI tail of each metadata tuple uninitialized.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic in `bio_integrity_prep()` is shown completely enough to decide. The root cause was that write-path integrity buffer allocation only used zeroed allocation when `bi->csum_type == BLK_INTEGRITY_CSUM_NONE`, which could leave the non-PI tail uninitialized for generated PI with `metadata_size > pi_tuple_size`. In this commit, the write case adds handling for `BLK_INTEGRITY_NOGENERATE`: `if (bi->flags & BLK_INTEGRITY_NOGENERATE) { if (bi_offload_capable(bi)) return true; set_flags = false; gfp |= __GFP_ZERO; } else if (bi->csum_type == BLK_INTEGRITY_CSUM_NONE) gfp |= __GFP_ZERO;`. This means when host metadata buffer allocation is required but generation is disabled, the buffer is explicitly zero-initialized via `gfp |= __GFP_ZERO`, preventing uninitialized metadata from being exposed. The helper `bi_offload_capable()` also distinguishes cases where controller offload is possible only when `tuple_size` matches the PI tuple size, matching the scenario described by the root cause (`metadata_size > pi_tuple_size` requires host buffer handling). Finally, generation is gated by `if (bio_data_dir(bio) == WRITE && bip_should_check(&bid->bip)) blk_integrity_generate(bio);`, so unchecked host buffers are not generated into, and zeroing is what makes them safe. Therefore the vulnerable construct is no longer present and the fix is present.
